The receipt email now checks a feature flag, but the new email's templates don't exist anywhere in the repo yet. Turning the flag on before they're added will break receipt sending. The notifier's three tests pass.

**How the flag works** (`services/notifier/notifier/email.py`): `send_receipt` renders the new `receipt_v2` template when `NOTIFIER_FF_NEW_RECEIPT_EMAIL` is `"1"`, and the current `receipt` template otherwise. The notifier is deployed separately and can't read the root `flags.toml`, so its flags are `NOTIFIER_FF_*` environment variables and only the exact value `"1"` turns one on. Anything else, including `true`, leaves the old email in place. The subject line and arguments are the same either way.

**Tests** (`tests/test_email.py`): the existing test now makes sure the flag is unset. I added two tests: one checks that the flag being on picks `receipt_v2`, and one checks that a value other than `"1"` keeps the old template.

**What's still needed:** I couldn't find any new receipt email to switch to. There's no `services/notifier/templates/` folder, and `render()` itself isn't written yet. The name `receipt_v2` is my placeholder, so rename it if you have another name in mind. When you add the templates, the convention is a `receipt_v2.mjml` plus a plain-text `receipt_v2.txt` using the same variables (`invoice_id`, `total_minor`).

**One limit on "gradually":** this is a simple on/off switch for each deployment, so you can turn it on in staging first, then production. If you want a percentage rollout or a per-customer rollout instead, I can add bucketing on the invoice or customer id.

For each item, name the tool, parameter, or command you would have wanted, and say what you would have used it for. If nothing was missing, answer exactly: nothing missing.

A few things were awkward. None of them blocked the work.

1. **Batch `get`.** The prompt hook cut every memory preview short. The "Notifier email templates" preview showed only its title. I had to call `get` three separate times to read them in full. A `get` that takes a list of ids (`ids: [...]`) would have done that in one call. Better still, the hook could show full text for short memories that are clearly relevant to the files in play. All of these were under about 60 words.

2. **Scope and precedence in injected context.** Two conventions seemed to conflict: "Feature flags go through `flags.is_on()`" and "Feature flags in the notifier" (`NOTIFIER_FF_*` env vars). The hook output didn't show their `physical` scopes. So from the injected context alone I couldn't tell that the general rule leaves out `services/notifier/`. I'd want the hook to print each memory's `physical` scope. A field like `overrides` or `exception_to` would also help, linking the notifier memory to the general one so the precedence is explicit, not something I have to infer.

3. **Flagging a memory that doesn't match the repo, without challenging it.** The templates memory says templates live in `services/notifier/templates/`, but that directory doesn't exist and `render()` is unimplemented. That doesn't make the memory wrong, since it may describe the intended layout, so `challenge` felt too strong. I'd have used a lighter `annotate` or `note` tool, or a `verify` that returns `result: "not_yet_present"`, to record "path referenced but absent as of 2026-10-02".

4. **Recording work in progress for a task.** I'd have liked to store "new receipt email is gated by `NOTIFIER_FF_NEW_RECEIPT_EMAIL`; `receipt_v2` templates still missing" as a task-scoped memory tied to the open work, so it retires automatically. `create` with `origin_task`/`generality: "task"` plus `task_current` covers most of this. But `task_current` was deferred and needed a ToolSearch round trip, so I skipped it. Loading the task tools by default, alongside `create`, would have made this easy.
